races.name: Macan At Porsche Centre Hull EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ard As A Rock
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who finished 9th and 5th over 6f on good — dropping to 5f here is a potential improvement angle, but David Evans' yard is 1/14 in 14 days and this horse has yet to win or place in two starts; needs clean early air to have any relevance.

runners_data.name: Mubehir
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Paul Midgley (0/21 T14) who ran 7th and 11th over 6f and 5f on good — the drop to 5f and move to hold-up tactics on a sharp track is a concern, but David Nolan's experience gives this runner the best possible chance of threading through late.

runners_data.name: Taj Mahal Palace
runners_data.note: Unraced and style unknown; Brian Ellison (2/15 T14) has debut form to respect and Beverley suits sharp, precocious types — must be respected purely on unexposed grounds but carries all the uncertainty of a first-time starter in a field with pace angles.

runners_data.name: True Charm
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman (3) rides a horse that has placed over 6f on good and drops in trip here — prominent style suits the scenario where the pace-duel leaves something to aim at, and three runs on similar going (0W1P) shows this filly handles conditions; 33 days off is not a concern at this level.

runners_data.name: Classy Jaguar
runners_data.note: The most likely pace-setter under Dougie Costello, with just one run (7th over 5f on good) suggesting experience is limited but Costello's front-running expertise could turn this into a controlled lead rather than a kamikaze one; Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood yard 1/8 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Desert Outlaw
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's second string (yard 0/21 T14) ran 6th and 9th over 5f and 6f on good — prominent style could place this horse nicely just off the three-way lead duel, though no win or place in two starts tempers expectations; Mark Winn takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Lexington Boom
runners_data.note: Two consecutive runner-up finishes over 5f on good make this the most exposed and consistent lead-type in the field — Oliver Stammers rides for Grant Tuer (0/5 T14), and if Lexington Boom can find the front without a destructive duel she could prove hard to pass, but two rivals equally keen to lead is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Mugheer
runners_data.note: Debutant from K.R. Burke (6/42 T14), unraced with style and going profile unknown — Burke's juveniles frequently debut with substantial improvement expected, and Clifford Lee is a capable handler of a green horse; must be treated as a serious unknown.

runners_data.name: Spectacular Diver
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby (4/60 T14) runner who placed over 5f on good and has form across three runs on similar ground — front-running style here but 70 days off is the headline query, and David Allan's experience should help sharpen focus on return; placed record (0W1P) shows ability to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Scottys Rocket
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's hold-up runner who finished 9th on debut over 5f on good and is tagged as fading in the finish — Cam Hardie rides but the combination of a single poor run, hold-up style over sharp 5f, and a fade pattern makes this one of the harder horses to support.

runners_data.name: Ubettabequeen
runners_data.note: Unraced Tim Easterby runner (4/60 T14) with unknown style and going profile — Sean Kirrane takes the mount and Easterby does produce well-drilled debut runners, but there is simply no form to anchor an assessment here.

runners_data.name: Needin' U
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse (Billy Garritty, Michael & David Easterby, 3/25 T14) who ran 4th over 5f and 11th over 6f on good — 67 days off and a hold-up profile over a flat 5f makes this tough to win unless the pace falls apart completely; headgear note (h) flagged.

runners_data.name: One More Tilda
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's (1/20 T14) debutant ridden by Tom Eaves — no form to assess and style unknown, with the trainer's modest recent strike rate offering little encouragement that this will be a significant first-time debut threat.

runners_data.name: Tiggywinkle
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears (0/5 T14) hold-up type who finished 10th over 6f on good debut and is flagged for fading in the finish — Jason Hart rides but the combination of a well-beaten single run, a fade tendency, and hold-up style over sharp 5f makes winning conditions very hard to construct.

races.paceDynamic: Beverley's sharp 5f on good-to-firm ground is a speed test from the gate, and with Classy Jaguar, Ard As A Rock, and Lexington Boom all confirmed front-runners among 14 runners, the early fractions will be genuinely contested rather than controlled. Classy Jaguar (Dougie Costello, experienced handler) is the most likely to dictate from stall position, but Ard As A Rock and Lexington Boom will dispute hard for the rail and early advantage, meaning the pace will be honest to strong rather than manufactured. The hold-up horses — Mubehir, Scottys Rocket, Needin' U, and Tiggywinkle — will need something to aim at late, but on a flat 5f track where lead-burners typically score even in strong-pace scenarios, the front-end horses burning each other out creates a legitimate window for a prominent or one-pace prominent type to pick up the pieces rather than a deep closer. The race shape most favours horses racing prominently just off the early speed who can sustain their effort through the final furlong, as pure front-runners risk blowing up in a three-way duel and genuine hold-up horses rarely get home in time over this sharp trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Burn, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace duel between Classy Jaguar, Ard As A Rock, and Lexington Boom is genuine and they take each other on relentlessly.
scenarios.body: The early leaders tie each other up through the first two furlongs and begin to empty inside the final furlong, leaving a horse travelling prominently just behind the pace to coast through. True Charm and Desert Outlaw both have the early pace to sit handy without over-committing, and on good-to-firm Beverley 5f this position is historically the race-winning one.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Classy Jaguar breaks quickest and the other two lead-types are unable to match stride early, allowing a solo, uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: Classy Jaguar under Costello dictates a controlled gallop rather than a suicide pace, conserving enough energy to quicken again inside the final furlong before the hold-up horses can close. Beverley's flat 5f actually rewards a horse that leads at a sensible clip, and with Costello's positional awareness this shape is entirely plausible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly brutal and every front-runner ties up entering the final furlong, creating a strong late run for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Mubehir (David Nolan, Paul Midgley) and Spectacular Diver have both placed over 5f on similar ground and could sweep through a tiring field if the sectionals are extreme. This scenario requires the pace to be genuinely ruinous — possible with three lead-types — but 5f at Beverley rarely gives deep closers enough racetrack to fully get home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut Talent Lands Blindside
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced runners — Mugheer, Taj Mahal Palace, Ubettabequeen, or One More Tilda — is significantly ahead of initial assessments.
scenarios.body: K.R. Burke's Mugheer and Brian Ellison's Taj Mahal Palace carry the strongest stable form credentials among the debutants, and a well-bred, well-prepared newcomer can exploit a muddled pace scenario on debut at a straightforward track. This remains the least predictable shape because running style and tactical positioning are entirely unknown.

watchPoints.text: Lexington Boom's two consecutive second-place finishes over 5f on good mark her as the standout exposed form-horse — if Classy Jaguar and Ard As A Rock burn each other up early, she may find a cleaner lead and prove very hard to peg back.

The three-way duel for the lead between Classy Jaguar, Ard As A Rock, and Lexington Boom in the opening furlong is the defining moment of the race — watch which of them blinks first, because the survivor who finds a rhythm could control everything from there.

Mugheer (K.R. Burke, Clifford Lee) and Taj Mahal Palace (Brian Ellison) are the two debutants whose stable credentials carry the most weight — either could land a serious debut blow and their early positioning in the stalls will signal how seriously connections have prepared them.

True Charm (Warren Fentiman 3, Lemos De Souza) steps back to 5f after placing over 6f on good — a prominent horse on a flat track with consistent going form who could be the biggest mover through a tiring pace scenario without attracting maximum market support.

Scottys Rocket and Tiggywinkle are both flagged for fading in finishes and carry hold-up profiles over a sharp 5f — if either drifts on course, it is likely reflecting market awareness of the tactical mismatch rather than any new information.

races.name: 911 At Porsche Centre Hull EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Clearanswer Call Centres Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for O'Meara and Tudhope who has struggled to make an impact in similar form figures of late (785056), and with 11 from 15 comparable-going runs yielding zero wins, needs everything to go right from the back.|

runners_data.name: Dabbling
runners_data.note: A 5-6f horse by recent profile stepping up to 7½f; three of last five runs were at 5f and the trip looks a significant stretch, weakening appeal despite decent handler form figures.|

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's 4yo holds the key tactical role as the sole front-runner; labelled as racing out of role at this trip but a 0.93 style fit still means he will likely stride to the front and set a sedate pace — his stamina beyond 6f is the main question on fast ground.|

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's 4yo has a headgear entry (p) and has won once in 15 similar-going runs; a genuine hold-up type squeezed into a midfield slot by field congestion, meaning he is unlikely to get the strongly-run race his form requires.|

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans' 3yo filly carries a hood (b) and has a strong record of placing (1W4P in similar going from five runs), suggesting she handles these conditions well; though a redistributed hold-up type, she is among the most likely to push forward and get competitive early.|

runners_data.name: The New Bay Pearl
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's 4yo mare carries top weight of 135lbs and has run four consecutive fourths over 8f on good ground — consistent but non-winning, and the drop back from 8f to 7½f is marginal; zero wins in 13 similar-going runs.|

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 4yo was a close third and second in recent runs (form 008293) and Tinkler's 5/29 14-day strike rate is respectable; 11 from 15 similar-going appearances suggest the conditions suit, and Alex Jary's 3lb claim provides a small pull on the weights.|

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 6yo has placed twice at 7f on good ground and twice gone close at this trip (form 022405); a genuine hold-up horse forced into a midfield map slot but is the most likely of the redistributed group to push for a prominent early position given his record.|

runners_data.name: Mickey Mongoose
runners_data.note: Olly Williams' 6yo last ran 67 days ago and has a hood (b); won over 7f on soft/standard but the 67-day absence is a notable concern, and while mapped to midfield he is a true backmarker who needs a truly-run race to fire.|

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: John Wainwright's 7yo veteran has run five consecutive placed or near-placed efforts at 8f on good ground (sim-going 9/15), but zero wins in those runs and now dropping to 7½f; a hold-up horse pushed forward by redistribution who may lack the pace for the sharper trip.|

runners_data.name: Furrst Lady
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 4yo is flagged for fading in finishes and has a 58-day absence; with just 4 from 6 relevant going runs and a sequence of mid-to-rear finishes, the tendency to weaken late is a serious concern and she is among the least likely to benefit from this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Ryefield
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's 3yo is also flagged as a fader, showing 10th, 8th, 8th, 5th in recent outings and failing to win in 9 similar-going tries; being mapped forward from a true hold-up position compounds the mismatch with this controlled pace.|

runners_data.name: Power Of Chora
runners_data.note: Jessica Macey's 3yo showed a decent 3rd over 5f at one point but recent form at 6-7f reads 8-0-6 and the step to 7½f looks ambitious; an inexperienced handler (T14: 0/2) further limits confidence.|

runners_data.name: Ganthorpe
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's 3yo won over 6f on good ground and has placed once in 13 similar-going runs; Joanna Mason takes the ride but the horse has run seven consecutive non-winning finishes since that win, and a hold-up type racing out of position limits prospects here.|

races.paceDynamic: Mister Sky Blue is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure from any horse capable of matching him stride for stride early — this sets up a controlled, rail-hugging lead at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Beverley's 7½f. The overwhelming majority of this field are true hold-up horses, and with King Sharja, Mickey Mongoose, Alice's Influence, Bantz, Ganthorpe and others all being redistributed from their natural rearward positions into the midfield map, the reality is that the bulk of the field will be tracking Mister Sky Blue at varying distances rather than pressuring him. The field holds significantly more hold-up and prominent-seeking horses than can realistically secure their preferred position, with King Sharja and Alice's Influence the likeliest to push forward and get close to Mister Sky Blue, while the genuine backmarkers will be forced further back than ideal. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured pace on fast ground — strongly favours any horse that can travel prominently in Mister Sky Blue's slipstream and produce a sustained finish in the straight, disadvantaging true hold-up types who need strong fractions to close the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Rails Run
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Sky Blue dictates alone at a fair pace and the prominent trackers cannot quicken past him in the straight.
scenarios.body: Mister Sky Blue sets an uncontested, economical gallop throughout and reaches the Beverley straight with a natural advantage over the hold-up pack; horses that have travelled close to him without expending energy are best placed to strike. The flat, fast surface suits those who can sustain their effort rather than needing a strongly-run race to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Mister Sky Blue in second or third covers the early pace without straining and then picks up decisively in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The leader sets a gallop that is comfortable but not dawdling, and a horse sitting just off him conserves energy to pounce; on Good to Firm Beverley the straight rewards those with stamina and a clean passage. Alice's Influence or King Sharja, both genuine prominent types forced into a tracking role, are best positioned to exploit this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Sky Blue goes too fast early for the conditions and weakens markedly entering the straight, opening the door for the midfield.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop would string the field out and leave the leader vulnerable, allowing horses with late energy to thread through; however, the majority of closers are redistributed hold-up types who may not be fully in their natural rhythm, limiting the potency of this shape. Sir David and Willowinghurn are the most credible beneficiaries given their genuine form in similar conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Finishing Kick From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compress the field and allow true backmarkers to close from outside the top half.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires fractions that simply may not materialise with a single front-runner and no pressing rivals; redistributed horses mapped to midfield are not truly positioned to deliver the late surge this shape demands. Mickey Mongoose, who has won off the pace at this trip on similar ground, is the only credible beneficiary if the race unfolds this way.

watchPoints.text: Mister Sky Blue's early positioning is the race pivot — watch whether he is allowed to stride to the front unchallenged, as any unexpected pressure from King Sharja or Alice's Influence could raise the tempo significantly and reshape the entire outcome.

King Sharja and Alice's Influence are both natural hold-up horses who may attempt to push forward in this single-pacemaker race; if both push for early prominence alongside Mister Sky Blue, the pace sharpens and the controlled-gallop scenario unravels.

Mickey Mongoose returns from 67 days off with a hood, and Furrst Lady comes back after 58 days — both are true hold-up types already out of position on the pace map, and their fitness on return adds a further layer of uncertainty to any late-running scenario.

Sir David's recent third at 7f on good ground (3/7f/GOO in last five) combined with the 3lb claim from Alex Jary makes him a tracker to monitor through the first half of the race — if he gets cover in midfield he could be travelling ominously when the field straightens up.

The going is officially Good to Firm for this race, confirmed by the going report; any significant drying during the card could further favour prominent-position horses who do not need to make up ground on an increasingly quick surface.

races.name: Jill Willows Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner with a win and four places in 15 Good-ground starts; Alistair Rawlinson takes over from the saddle and Grant Tuer's yard is currently misfiring (0/5 in 14 days), so the tactical threat is real but the stable's form tempers confidence.|

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a major booking upgrade and Michael Dods has a winner in the last 14 days; this hold-up horse has a course win at the trip and seven Good-ground runs suggest he handles conditions, though he will need the pace to truly collapse to get involved from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner returning from 89 days off, which is a notable freshness flag; headgear (tongue tie) is retained and she has two wins and four places in similar ground, but the layoff and the pace battle she will face make it difficult for her to dominate as she would prefer.|

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard is among the busiest in the data (5/43 in 14 days) and this 4-year-old has a consistent pattern of placing prominently on Good ground; ran just four days ago which raises a fitness versus freshness question, but the style and record at this trip are solid.|

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 82, with two wins and six places from 11 Good-ground starts; Conor Whiteley claims 5lb which is a significant advantage for a horse carrying 144lbs, and a blinkers-on profile suggests he needs to be held up briefly before being produced — perfect for a pace-collapse scenario.|

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in his finishes and his recent form reads 01550, suggesting he finds the line elusive; Jason Hart is an experienced handler of hold-up horses and Julie Camacho has a winner recently, but the finishing-fade concern is hard to dismiss on this demanding track.|

runners_data.name: Bell Shot
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner with one of the highest ORs in the field (81) and Mason Paetel claims 5lb; Michael Appleby also trains Intervention, and Bell Shot's best efforts have come racing prominently — he is one of the two most likely to actually secure the early lead ahead of the pack.|

runners_data.name: Flying Fletcher
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey have three winners in 14 days which is a positive stable flag; this hold-up horse steps back up in trip having run over 10f last time, and his Good-ground figures (6 runs, 0 wins, 1 place) make him a fringe player at best in a strongly-run race.|

runners_data.name: Beyond The Bar
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old with a front-running style taking on older horses; David Allan is a canny pilot around Beverley but the horse's recent form shows more defeats than wins at this trip and conditions, and he is likely to be squeezed out of his natural position by the more powerful front-runners.|

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison has two winners in 14 days and this 3-year-old has an excellent record on Good ground (3 wins, 7 places from 10 runs); he sits prominently by nature and the claimer Ben Robinson (no allowance listed but a handy booking) suits the front-tracking role this race shape rewards.|

runners_data.name: Intervention
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 9-year-old is a genuine hold-up operator by preference, but with more closers than the map can accommodate, he ends up shown in midfield — a position that is not his natural race territory. His recent form (008770) and zero wins from 15 Good-ground runs make him a very marginal participant regardless of where he settles, and the style-fit discount applies firmly.|

races.paceDynamic: Bell Shot, Highland Olly, Style Of Life, and Beyond The Bar all want to lead, guaranteeing a strong, honest gallop from the outset over Beverley's 7½f on Good to Firm ground — this is not a race where any single horse will dictate unchallenged. The pace war up front will string the field out early, burning off the leaders' reserves before they reach the final two furlongs, and the relentless gallop will place a genuine premium on stamina over raw speed. Prominent horses who can tuck in just off the breakneck pace — particularly Alpha Capture and Tattie Bogle — are ideally placed to inherit a weakening lead without having expended the same energy. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile: horses who settle just behind a contested lead and produce a sustained, grinding finish rather than a sharp sprint. The field holds more front-running types than can all secure their natural position; Bell Shot and Highland Olly, with the highest OR and most recent front-running form respectively, are the most likely to actually boss the early gallop, with Style Of Life and Beyond The Bar forced to either capitulate early or race wider and higher than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way lead battle burns out the front-runners, leaving the prominent trackers to come through in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Bell Shot, Highland Olly, Style Of Life, and Beyond The Bar fight for supremacy through the first half, creating a punishing tempo that collapses their late reserves; Alpha Capture and Tattie Bogle, sitting just off the pace, are perfectly positioned to pick up the pieces in the closing stages. This shape overwhelmingly suits prominent horses with proven form on Good to Firm who can sustain their effort rather than sprint — both Alpha Capture and Tattie Bogle fit that bill precisely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Bell Shot or Highland Olly breaks decisively and establishes a commanding lead while rivals are slow to respond.
scenarios.body: One horse secures a clear advantage through the first couple of furlongs and is allowed to bowl along at a controlled pace rather than being hounded into a punishing duel, preserving enough in the tank to hold on; this scenario demands a genuine front-runner with course-distance form on this ground. Bell Shot's recent record of placing from the front and Highland Olly's natural galloping style make them the primary candidates if a gap opens up early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly relentless and the entire field is strung out, allowing a well-ridden midfield horse to finish strongest.
scenarios.body: Glenfinnan, who has course form and is handled by Daniel Tudhope, is capable of threading through late if the race degenerates into a genuine stamina test; Homestrait, a natural prominent racer with impressive Good ground figures, could also time a run to perfection if the leaders tie each other up. This shape requires the pace to be genuinely unsustainable rather than merely fast, which is not guaranteed even with multiple front-runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so extreme that the entire race implodes in the final furlong, gifting late-running hold-up horses a rare opening.
scenarios.body: Obelix and Glenfinnan would theoretically benefit from a complete implosion, but both carry form concerns — Obelix is flagged as fading in finishes and Intervention, the most natural hold-up type in the field, has been redistributed to midfield and is racing out of role with poor recent form. This is the least likely scenario because genuine, effective hold-up horses are thin on the ground here, and Intervention's style-fit discount further erodes the probability.

watchPoints.text: Bell Shot and Highland Olly are on a collision course for the lead — watch whether either blinks early; if one capitulates inside the first two furlongs, the other may control a more sensible pace and the dynamics shift entirely toward the leader.

Style Of Life returns from 89 days off and will need to travel well from the outset to justify a front-running role — monitor her behaviour in the stalls and early in the race, as a sluggish start would render her racing style completely redundant.

Alpha Capture is carrying top weight (144lbs) but Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim offsets this considerably — if he is given a clear run to emerge from the prominent group in the final two furlongs, his OR of 82 makes him dangerous and this claim advantage could be race-deciding.

Tattie Bogle ran just four days ago, which is an unusually short turnaround — watch whether she moves freely in the paddock and whether Andrew Mullen opts to hold her up slightly more than normal to compensate for any residual fatigue.

Glenfinnan's headgear entry (h — hood) combined with a Daniel Tudhope booking is a market-watch signal; if he is supported in the ring, Tudhope may have been given specific tactical instructions to work the Good to Firm ground from a handy position rather than his usual hold-up role.

races.name: Cayenne Electric At Porsche Centre Hull Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bearwith
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a genuine winning run just 18 days ago over 10f on standard ground; the step up to 1m2f on fast going looks fine but the controlled pace set by Ciao Capo will make it hard to peel off the back and close from last.|

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee rides this five-year-old who has three placings from seven runs in similar going and whose prominent style puts him in the perfect position to track Ciao Capo and strike; the headgear (tp) suggests connections are keeping him switched on, and 1m2f on good-to-firm is no concern.|

runners_data.name: Ciao Capo
runners_data.note: The race's single confirmed front-runner, trained by Richard and Peter Fahey with two wins from three starts over a mile on good ground; though flagged as racing slightly out of optimal role by style-fit metrics, with nobody to press him the question is whether he can translate that lead into a winning margin over this longer trip.|

runners_data.name: Dr Rio
runners_data.note: A decade-old campaigner whose natural hold-up style is his trademark — genuinely one of the true backmarkers here but shuffled forward on the map because too many closers compete for the same space; his two wins from twelve fast-ground starts show he can run into form, but the pace scenario does him few favours today.|

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Consistent placed filly whose last five runs are all in the frame at 8-10f on good ground, and wearing a p headgear to keep her focused; she'll try to sit in mid-pack and pick up late but needs something to go wrong up front to feature, given the likely modest gallop.|

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's mare is racing just seven days after her last outing and carries headgear (p); her form line of 444232 shows remarkable consistency around placed positions, and she excels in good-to-firm conditions with five C&D-relevant placings — but her natural closer's role is squeezed by the pace map and she needs a stronger pace than Ciao Capo is likely to set.|

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner at this trip and grade, trained by Easterby alongside Sunny Orange, with David Allan taking the ride; his prominent style suits the race shape directly, the 14-day turnaround is positive for a horse in form, and good-to-firm has historically been his playground with six places from nine such starts.|

runners_data.name: Langton Wold
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's seven-year-old wears tongue-tie and has his best form over much longer distances — 16f and 17f — making this 1m2f trip a potential stamina undershoot; his natural hold-up instincts are compressed into a midfield slot on the map with several others, and his OR of 48 means he carries least weight but also has least form at this level.|

races.paceDynamic: Ciao Capo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 1m2f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Beverley, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Oisin Orr can dictate matters at whatever tempo suits the three-year-old. That uncontested lead on a flat track with fast ground sets up a sustainable, controlled gallop rather than a scorching early pace, which historically favours the horse on or near the front rather than those making up ground from the rear. The field carries a significant cluster of hold-up types — Dr Rio, Sunny Orange, and Langton Wold are genuine closers who have been mapped into midfield positions simply because there is no room for them all to sit at the back in this race shape; the runners most likely to actually secure a prominent position behind Ciao Capo are No Knee Never and Kitsune Power, with Princess Niyla likely tucking in just behind them. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled, single-pace gallop on fast ground with Ciao Capo dictating from the front strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce, with true hold-up horses disadvantaged by the absence of a strong pace to chase down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ciao Capo Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ciao Capo is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and sets a measured gallop that never fully unwinds the closers.
scenarios.body: Oisin Orr controls fractions from the front on good-to-firm going that rewards toe-in-the-ground types, and with no one willing to press, the three-year-old's recent winning form over course-relevant distances makes this a serious winning prospect; the prominent trackers No Knee Never and Kitsune Power are best placed to pick up the scraps.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ciao Capo sets a slightly more pressured pace and the prominent trackers No Knee Never and Kitsune Power time their runs to sweep past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: No Knee Never (headgear, good-to-firm record) and Kitsune Power (last-time winner over C&D trip) are both proven prominent types who thrive on fast ground and carry sufficient form to overhaul a tiring leader; both have the class ceiling to win a race of this grade if delivered at the right moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or quickens late enough to create a gap through tired horses for a closer to exploit.
scenarios.body: Sunny Orange boasts five places from twelve starts in similar going and has the acceleration to finish strongly if the race develops gaps late, while Bearwith has course-and-distance placed form and could benefit if the prominent types all burn out simultaneously; however, all three redistributed closers are operating out of their ideal position and face a tough ask against a controlled pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles The Field
scenarios.trigger: If Ciao Capo is deliberately crowded or unseated from its rhythm early, causing the pace to become ragged and unpredictable.
scenarios.body: In a messy, stop-start race with no settled order, Bearwith's proven ability to stay and finish from off the pace could come into its own, while Princess Niyla's consistent placed form in running suggests she handles disrupted gallops without losing her head; this scenario remains unlikely given the small field and clear pace advantage held by one runner.

watchPoints.text: Ciao Capo's early lead is the race's pivot point — if Oisin Orr gets a soft lead unchallenged, monitor whether No Knee Never or Kitsune Power tracks close enough to mount a real challenge in the final two furlongs.

Kitsune Power's rapid 14-day return and in-form trainer angle (4/60 in 14 days) make him a live threat under David Allan if he settles close to the pace — watch for him to be produced travelling well entering the straight.

Sunny Orange ran just seven days ago and her true closer's instincts will be blunted by the controlled Ciao Capo gallop; if she loses her position early or gets boxed behind midfielders, her chance evaporates before the race reaches its critical phase.

Langton Wold's best performances have come over marathon trips of 16-17f, making this 1m2f trip short of his optimum — watch for him to be outpaced before the straight rather than finishing with his usual staying surge.

The going report confirms good-to-firm across the card at Beverley rather than the declared good, which tilts the premium further toward horses with fast-ground form — check that no last-minute ground-related rider or trainer withdrawals reshape the pace map before the off.

races.name: Nation Radio Yorkshire Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Twice a winner over this course and distance on good ground in recent runs, she brings excellent course and going form for Ruth Carr, and her hold-up style requires a fast pace to deliver her finish — a controlled tempo from Hanney Girl is her biggest obstacle.

runners_data.name: Straight Ahead
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners this lightly-framed three-year-old whose two wins both came at five furlongs on standard or soft ground; 27 days off is not a concern, but she has yet to prove she handles good-to-firm convincingly and her hold-up style is reliant on pace developing ahead.

runners_data.name: Hanney Girl
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field, wearing a hood, and trained by the in-form Tim Easterby yard; her recent form figures on good ground are modest but she sets the pace parameters for the entire race and an uncontested lead over five flat furlongs plays entirely to her advantage.

runners_data.name: Qila
runners_data.note: Had just one run in similar going and showed placed form over five furlongs on good, but Brian Ellison sends her here on a quick five-day turnaround and her hold-up profile means she needs gaps to open late — redistribution pressure in the prominent group may not create that opportunity.

runners_data.name: Kilfrush Desert
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form with two seconds and a third in only three career runs, all at six furlongs on good or standard; the drop to five furlongs here is untested and her unknown running style makes it hard to predict where she will settle, though a flexible profile could be an asset if the race is messy.

runners_data.name: Rumble Ruby
runners_data.note: Won over six furlongs on good ground for this small yard and Warren Fentiman claims 3lb, making the weight attractive; she is a genuine prominent type who should travel close to Hanney Girl, and her recent win at six suggests stamina is not a concern if the pace is modest.

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Two wins over five furlongs on good ground and a placed run at the same track give Dragon Spin strong race-fit credentials; Dougie Costello is an experienced jockey who will look to park him prominently, and his proven ability to quicken over this trip is a key asset.

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: A runner with an impressive 10/10 record in similar going conditions, including two wins over five and six furlongs on good ground; Mark Winn will aim to place him handily, and Simba's Pride's consistency in this going profile makes him one of the more reliable prominent-type profiles.

runners_data.name: Lamlash Bay
runners_data.note: A winner over six furlongs on good ground for the Michael & David Easterby partnership and apprentice Lewis Chalkley takes the 7lb claim; dropping back to five furlongs is a question mark given all her form has come over six, and she may find the trip too sharp at this pace.

runners_data.name: Black Missile
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's runner has placed form at six furlongs on good ground but his natural instinct is to race prominently — with Dragon Spin, Simba's Pride, Rumble Ruby, and Lamlash Bay all competing for the same real estate, he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal and his chance must be tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Under The Radar
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse from Tim Easterby's yard whose last two runs produced thirds over five furlongs on good ground, suggesting ability if the pace serves; mapped to midfield due to field composition, his true rear-of-field role means the controlled pace Hanney Girl is likely to set represents a significant disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Hanney Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, David Allan can dictate terms from the gates at whatever tempo he chooses on good-to-firm ground over Beverley's straight five. Behind her, Dragon Spin, Simba's Pride, Rumble Ruby, and Lamlash Bay will contest the prominent berths, creating a moderately competitive early order that nonetheless stops well short of a true pace battle — meaning Hanney Girl is unlikely to be pressured into setting a searching gallop. The field holds more prominent-minded types than can all secure their preferred position; Black Missile is a natural prominent racer who will be squeezed into a midfield slot, and Under The Radar is a genuine hold-up horse similarly displaced, so neither should be assessed purely on their mapped position. A controlled, single-paced tempo benefits horses that can travel handy and grind out a finish — the prominent runners who can sit just off Hanney Girl without expending energy fighting for position are best placed, while true hold-up horses will need an unlikely finishing burst on what is an essentially flat, sprint track with minimal late-race compression.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hanney Girl Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hanney Girl bowls clear unchallenged and the prominent pack cannot close the gap on a sound surface.
scenarios.body: Hanney Girl settles into an uncontested rhythm, dictating a pace she is comfortable with, and the lack of pressure means she never ties up late; on good-to-firm Beverley five furlongs this suits a front-runner who can conserve energy and sprint again in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet Dragon Spin, Simba's Pride, Rumble Ruby, and Lamlash Bay push hard early and overwhelm Hanney Girl inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace is taken up by the front-runner but the chasing prominent group travel close enough to pounce once the sprint begins in earnest; horses with strong recent form on good ground and proven ability over five furlongs are advantaged here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and Angel Numbers or Straight Ahead produce a sustained late charge from the rear.
scenarios.body: Angel Numbers has won twice over this course and distance on good ground and carries strong recent form, giving her the profile to close fastest if the front-runners tire; Straight Ahead's two wins at five furlongs also give her a chance in this shape, though neither is guaranteed space or a clean run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Early Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse to be restrained and create a faster-than-expected early gallop that brings the field together.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish suits horses with tactical versatility and good recent condition; Kilfrush Desert's consistent placed form at this level and Qila's ability to race prominently give them each a slim chance if the race turns messy and unpredictable.

watchPoints.text: Hanney Girl's uncontested lead is the single biggest pace factor in this race — if David Allan is allowed to stride clear without challenge from the prominent group, she could prove very difficult to reel in over this flat five furlongs.

Dragon Spin and Simba's Pride are both genuine prominent types who will attempt to sit second or third — watch the first furlong to see which of them establishes the better position, as the runner who settles closest to Hanney Girl without burning energy will be best placed for the final dash.

Black Missile is a natural prominent racer who is likely to be squeezed wide or back in the early stages given the number of prominent rivals — monitor his early positioning at the stalls; if he fails to secure a forward berth, his chance diminishes materially.

Angel Numbers has strong course and distance form but needs a brisk tempo to deliver her hold-up finish — watch whether the pace is strong enough in the first two furlongs to create the gap she needs late, as this is the key condition for her getting involved.

Lamlash Bay's 7lb apprentice claim (Lewis Chalkley) makes her competitive on weight, but all her prior form is over six furlongs — watch whether she shows any signs of being outpaced in the first two furlongs at Beverley, which would confirm the trip is too sharp.
